new_statements.quote: NASALIZAÇÃO: Todas as vogais podem ser nasalizadas e quando o forem receberão um til (~). SÍLABA TÔNICA: Na maioria das vezes, é a última sílaba da palavra. Por isso, só usamos o acento quando ele recai em outra sílaba. Acentuamos também o hiato (ex.: aí). Acentuamos a primeira vogal de ditongo com vogal nasal, quando esta não fôr a acentuada (ex.: éĩ).
new_statements.translation: NASALIZATION: All vowels can be nasalized and when they are they receive a tilde (~). STRESSED SYLLABLE: In most cases it is the last syllable of the word. For that reason we write the accent mark only when it falls on another syllable. We also mark hiatus (e.g. aí). We put an accent on the first vowel of a diphthong with a nasal vowel when that vowel is not the stressed one (e.g. éĩ).
new_statements.citation: Orlandi, Eni P. 1982. 'Critérios empregados na definição da grafia'. In: Silva, Aracy Lopes da; Santos, Leinad Ayer O; Luz, Mara L. Manzoni (eds.), Lições de Bahetá: sobre a língua Pataxó Hãhãhãi. São Paulo: Comissão Pró-Índio de São Paulo, 56 pp.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: The quotation was checked again. Opened (55-page image scan, no text layer; CPI-SP open URL). Viewed the page render / PDF p.5, 'Criterios empregados na definicao da grafia', signed 'Eni P. Orlandi, Universidade Estadual de Campinas'). The passage is there exactly as quoted: 'NASALIZACAO: Todas as vogais podem ser nasalizadas e quando o forem receberao um til (~). SILABA TONICA: Na maioria das vezes, e a ultima silaba da palavra. Por isso, so usamos o acento quando ele recai em outra silaba. Acentuamos tambem o hiato (ex.: ai). Acentuamos a primeira vogal de ditongo com vogal nasal, quando esta nao for a acentuada (ex.: ei).' (diacritics as in the reader's quote; the scanned. page 05 garble…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the final syllable in the majority of the 129 recorded words; non-final stress occurs in a minority of items and is marked in the practical orthography with a written accent.
new_statements.exceptions: 'Na maioria das vezes' -- some words have stress on a non-final syllable; these are the ones written with an accent mark in the booklet's word pages (no list or count given in the criteria text).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level ('sílaba da palavra'); based on isolated citation forms (129 words, 2 sentences) elicited from a single elderly rememberer (Bahetá, Itaju do Colônia, Bahia, 1982; researchers G. Urban and A. Lopes da Silva; orthography by E. P. Orlandi at IEL/Unicamp from the phonetic transcriptions and tapes). An orthography note, not a phonological analysis.
new_statements.identity_note: Statement concerns Pataxó Hãhãhãe proper (pata1261, 'Pataxó Setentrional'), as remembered by the last speaker Bahetá in 1982 (129 words, 2 sentences) -- not the revitalized Patxohã used today by the Pataxó people (which Nikulin 2020 treats as unclassifiable) and not Wied's Pataxó Meridional. The source is an orthography-criteria note in a community booklet, written by a linguist (E. P. Orlandi) from phonetic transcriptions and tapes; it is first-hand but not a phonological analysis, and the corpus is terminal-speaker citation forms.

new_statements.quote: p. 32: "La tribu Hahaháy, qui parle un dialecte du Nord de la langue Patašo, vivait originairement sur le rio Cachoeira, État de Bahia. [...] Le vocabulaire manuscrit de Nimuendajú (84) s'est perdu, mais dans les archives du prof. Darcy Ribeiro, à Rio de Janeiro, j'ai copié quelques mots d'un autre vocabulaire Patašo du Nord, recueilli par Scheibe (104)." Wordlist entries (Hahaháy column): "arbre mihná / arc pokái / dent an-tóy / étoile maɲũhá / femme bektiá / feu itahábm / flèche pohóy / homme kahnãkó / main am-pahábm / maison mbahikó" (p. 32); "manger ko-má / œil ã-guá / pied am-paká / poisson mahám / tabac kahábm / terre hahám / tête am-akoháy / 3 mouɲhí"; but "crocodile emáio", "oiseau pekáynão" (p. 33).
new_statements.translation: p. 32: "The Hahaháy tribe, which speaks a northern dialect of the Patašo language, originally lived on the rio Cachoeira, State of Bahia. [...] Nimuendajú's manuscript vocabulary (84) is lost, but in the archives of Prof. Darcy Ribeiro in Rio de Janeiro I copied a few words from another Northern Patašo vocabulary, collected by Scheibe (104)." Entries: tree mihná / bow pokái / tooth an-tóy / star maɲũhá / woman bektiá / fire itahábm / arrow pohóy / man kahnãkó / hand am-pahábm / house mbahikó; eat ko-má / eye ã-guá / foot am-paká / fish mahám / tobacco kahábm / earth hahám / head am-akoháy / three mouɲhí; but crocodile emáio, bird pekáynão.
new_statements.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1963. Documents et vocabulaires inédits de langues et de dialectes sud-américains. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 52: 7-60 (Scheibe 1957 Pataxó list, pp. 32-33).

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Read and Persée renderPage images) directly. p. 32 heading '28. — Hahaháy.' and the prose quote ('La tribu Hahaháy, qui parle un dialecte du Nord de la langue Patašo, vivait originairement sur le rio Cachoeira, État de Bahia. [..] Le vocabulaire manuscrit de Nimuendajú (84) s'est perdu, mais dans les archives du prof. Darcy Ribeiro, à Rio de Janeiro, j'ai copié quelques mots d'un autre vocabulaire Patašo du Nord, recueilli par Scheibe (104).') are verbatim on the image. Wordlist forms match the image; two minor transcription differences: image has 'pohóy n' (superscript n after the form) where the reader wrote 'pohóy', and 'emáïo' (diaeresis on i) where the reader wrote 'emáio'. Count verif…
new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the catalog's final-stress record and with Orlandi 1982 ('Na maioria das vezes, é a última sílaba da palavra'): the accented forms in Scheibe's list are overwhelmingly final, with the same kind of minority non-final cases Orlandi allows for. It is an accent-marked wordlist without a legend, so it supports rather than states the rule. The Persée PDF (docAsPDF) was refused twice (not reachable by automated download 'protected by altcha'); the pages were read from Persée's own renderPage viewer images (1358x2184 grayscale) and scanned with tesseract eng (diacritics unreliable; quotes transcribed against the images).
new_statements.rule_in_words: No prose statement on stress anywhere in the article's front matter or in the Pataxó sections; the only evidence is the acute accent in the 40-item Hahaháy list, which Loukotka uses without a legend. Of the roughly 30 accented forms, all but two (emáio 'crocodile', pekáynão 'bird', penultimate) carry the acute on the last syllable; about ten forms carry no accent at all (mip'oi, pahasi, a, an-tõhũ, pahog, eɲakčẽi, anày, maɲu, abakače, abače). Taken as stress marks, the data point to final-syllable stress with occasional penultimate exceptions - inferred from a secondary copy of Scheibe's list, not stated.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; in the list, emáio 'crocodile' and pekáynão 'bird' are accented on the penult, and several items carry no accent.
new_statements.identity_note: Loukotka 1963 §28 'Hahaháy' is explicitly 'un dialecte du Nord de la langue Patašo' whose last survivors were found by Nimuendajú at the SPI post Paraguaçu (Bahia), i.e. the Pataxó Hãhãhãe of pata1261; the list is Loukotka's copy of Scheibe's manuscript from Darcy Ribeiro's archives, not a field record. The adjacent §27 'Monačobm ou Monošo' (pp. 30-31, Nimuendajú 1940) is a different Bahian variety and was not used. The catalog's existing statement (Orlandi 1982) rests on Bahetá's 129 words recorded in 1982 at Itaju do Colônia.
